events.text: Illuskan seafarers from Ruathym began settling the various islands of the Trackless Sea. They come to fear and avoid the mischievous fey of the Moonshae Isles, thinking the islands to be cursed.
cites: Dragon 362: Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes, с. 23–31

events.text: The Keryjek Wars were the only serious conflict to occur on the Great Glacier among the Ulutiun peoples.

The humans known as the Nar, fleeing from the armies of the Nentyarch, enter a portal in Ashanath. Their King Arkaius sacrifices himself and seals the portal behind their escape. The tribe settles in the Council Hills in the Shaar and rename themselves the Arkaiun after their martyred monarch
cites: Shining South, с. 103

events.text: By the -900 DR, the two emergent nations had significantly risen in power and engaged escalating conflicts with one another.
cites: Old Empires, с. 5

events.text: In -750 DR, the Netherese had moved to Melairbode uninvited, and made their home adjacent to the dwarves.
In -681 DR, arcanists who came to be known as the Night Parade, traveled to the Demiplane of Nightmares which was scantly protected by the aberrations of the Far Realm.
By -626 DR this area including the Windy Plains was once again dominated by goblin tribes.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 44–45

events.text: In the Year of Oaths Forsaken, -626 DR, Narfell and Raumathar entered into a struggle for control over the lands surrounding Lake Ashane.
In -623 DR, Raumathar surprised its neighbor Narfell by attacking them while they were being beaten in a war with Mulhorand, beginning the first of many wars with the Nar people.

Most of the Fey, including the fomorians, abandoned their domains in the Moonshaes and retreated back into the Feywild. The kingdom of Sarifal is abandoned and the city of Karador sinks into the Myrloch.
cites: Dragon 362: Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes, с. 23–31

events.text: In the Year of Imparted Riches, -469 DR, the population of Songfarla was dwindling until four svirfneblin clans migrated there, the Covarrkar, Fungusfoot, Glasszhorm, and Longstepper clans.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 43

events.text: In -461 DR they began draining both life and magic from both Toril and the floating enclaves, creating barren wastelands where there once were lush fields and areas of wild magic.
Circa -350 DR, the migration of Netherese refugees to Illusk reached its peak as settlers from towns across Low Netheril move westward to escape the depredations of the phaerimms.
In the Year of Bold Poachers, -349 DR, Saldrinar destroyed Kisonraathiisar and became Westgate's first human king.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 47

events.text: In -345 DR, Arthindol the Terraseer appeared in the enclave of Eileanar with a warning that goddess Mystryl would challenge Netheril in a manner never before seen.
cites: Lost Empires of Faerûn, с. 98

events.text: In the year -343 DR, Dareth was attacked by white dragons and their bestial servant creatures from Hoarfaern after breaking into the dragon's caverns unleashing a brutal war between the realms.
The Fall of Netheril. The transformation of Mystryl to Mystra.
cites: Netheril: Empire of Magic: The Winds of Netheril, с. 12

events.text: Karsus's Folly was a climactic event that caused the end of the Netherese empire in -339 DR.
Mystra's Ban was a decree that the goddess Mystra made about the mortal use of powerful magic.
In -331 DR, the Land Under Shadow was freed by the forces of Cormanthor, which included the armies of Cormanthyr and Rystall Wood and a group of Eilistraee-worshiping drow.
In -318 DR a final climactic confrontation was made on the broad mountaintop now known as Heroes' Height, where the last of the Darethian dwarves fell.
cites: Dwarves Deep, с. 55

events.text: In the Year of Foul Awakenings, -286 DR, the vampire Orlak and a small army of mercenaries captured the city in a single night.
In Year of Overflowing Casks, -276 DR, a new and dominant force emerged in Jhaamdath, as the powerful metamind Dharien overthrew the nation's bladelords and declared himself emperor of Jhaamdath.
Jhaamdath falls.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 51

events.text: In -255 DR, Hlundite warriors destroyed the city of Monikar after it brutally slew Netherese refugees after offering them shelter.
cites: Netheril: Empire of Magic: The Winds of Netheril, с. 80

events.text: In the Year of Furious Waves, -255 DR, they called forth a cataclysmic tidal wave from the Jhaamdath Bay, instantly destroying all of the Twelve Cities of the Sword.
In the Year of the Striking Lance, -247 DR, Tyr, god of justice and war, emerged from a portal at Beansidhe Hill near what would later be Alaghôn in Turmish.
The Procession of Justice was a campaign to pacify the remnants of the fallen empire of Jhaamdath in the Vilhon Reach in the mid–3rd century DR.

By this year the city enjoyed four thousand years of prosperity. It passed into its sixth rysar as Eltargrim Irithyl emerged as the newest Coronal. Due to the increasing threat of regular orc raids and the greater influence held by other races of Faerûn, Coronal Eltagrim declared that a mythal would be built around the city and allowed the first human visitor to set foot within.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 53
Cormanthyr: Empire of the Elves, с. 35
The Return of Randal Morn, с. 4

events.text: During his early reign, he dealt with the orc problem of Rystall Wood, which found itself invaded in -205 DR.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 53

events.text: The Passing of Power took place in -205 DR when the elf Iliphar Nelnueve challenged the black dragon Thauglor to a Feint of Honor.
By the Year of Sunned Serpents, −189 DR, Serpentes had conquered all Lapaliiya, the Tashalar, and the surrounding lands, with Ormpur alone remaining free.

The Eye Tyrant Wars, known as the Orb Marches in Calimshan and the Deathsphere Battles by the dwarves, were a series of constant battles in the east of the Lands of Intrigue during the Fifth Age of Calimshan, in which the humans of Tethyr and Calimshan allied with the dwarves and humans of Iltkazar against the beholders of the Alimir Mountains and their armies.
The Great Conflagration was a decade-long cataclysm that occurred between the nations of Narfell and Raumathar between -160 DR and -150 DR.
In the Year of the Stone Giant, -160 DR, Narfell and Raumathar entered into what would become their final war, known centuries later as the Great Conflagration.
cites: Lost Empires of Faerûn, с. 62

events.text: In -160 DR, a cairn by the title of Dodkong came to to the site of the fallen kingdom with the crown of Obadai, the legendary crown of Faerûn's first stone giant, and gathered its stone giants clans together, refounding the kingdom under the name of Cairnheim.
cites: Underdark, с. 133
Drizzt Do'Urden's Guide to the Underdark, с. 85
Lost Empires of Faerûn, с. 115

events.text: In -160 DR, the last of these wars, which came to be known as the Great Conflagration, began with the summoning of the avatar of Kostchtchie and his frost giant armies from the Icerim Mountains.

In thanks for Tethyr's participation in the Eye Tyrant Wars, the Pasha of Calimshan granted King Silvam Ithal the lands of Mir wholesale in -150 DR, also titling him the Raj of Ankaram (this also disarmed the disloyal Raj of Mir who was planning rebellion).
cites: Empires of the Shining Sea, с. 21
Lands of Intrigue: Tethyr, с. 27

events.text: In eons past, the lands of Thesk were once part of the empire of Narfell, but little survived the Great Conflagration that destroyed that empire in the Year of Recompense, -150 DR.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 57

events.text: The Jhaamdathan refugee Impil Mirandor, founded the settlement of Impil's Tor atop the abandoned dwarfhold of Felimar.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 57

events.text: Impil's Tor was renamed Lyrabar by Ornrath Mirandor. The thriving settlement managed to open trade talks with the nearby dwarven clans.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 57

events.text: In the Year of Terrible Anger, -111 DR, the Delzoun fell prey to the same orc assaults that devastated other kingdoms of the North, when orcs launched simultaneous attacks from their caverns caverns in the Spine of the World, abandoned mines in the Graypeaks, from lost dwarfholds in the Ice Mountains, from cairn complexes in the Nether Mountains, and upward from the depts of the High Moon Mountains, though the kingdom endured for few more years.
cites: Lost Empires of Faerûn, с. 84
Lost Empires of Faerûn, с. 88

events.text: In -111 DR, Iliyanbruen helped the settlements of the North against the Orc Marches.

In the Year of Terrible Anger, -111 DR, a massive orc horde streamed out of the Spine of the World and laid waste to the Kingdom of Illusk and the hidden city of Gauntlgrym, and ravaged the dwarven empire of Delzoun.
The Orc Marches was the name given to one of the biggest orc conquests of the North.

In the Year of the Valorous Kobold, -106 DR, during one of the last battles of the War, a legion of elite morkoth warriors slew the storm giant adventurer Lorthan and took from him the legendary double-bladed sword Krakenscourge.
In the Year of the Spiked Gauntlet, -102 DR, hin were said to had followed a ghostwise cleric Desva, adopting the deity's bloodthirsty ways.
The Hin Ghostwar (also known as the Hin Ghostwars and the Ghost War) was a long conflict between the ghostwise halflings and the allied strongheart and lightfoot halflings in the Lluirwood in Luiren.
In the Year of the Black Unicorn, -100 DR, as the great underground northkingdom of Delzoun fell around them, Citadel Sundbarr was saved by the ingenuity of its master forgers.
Inrath Mirandor established the kingdom of Old Impiltur. His coronation marks the founding of the Mirandor Dynasty.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 59

events.text: In the -68 DR, Chand, a strongheart halfling hunter chieftain made an alliance with the leaders of the lightfoots.
In the Year of the Raging Brook, -45 DR, the pharaoh of Mulhorand decided to annex Rashemen, and sent a huge army through the Gorge of Gauros.
In the Year of Harpist's Delight, -33 DR, Asram was struck by a horrendous plague.
In -15 DR, the Grand Cabal of Illusk would be taken by imperial urges to expand their borders southward and eastward.
By -12 DR they would find their southward expansion efforts halted by Iliyanbruen.
In the Year of Burning Glades, -10 DR, Lord Halueth Never, a sun elf hero, led the elves of Iliyanbruen to victory over Illusk.
In -4 DR, the leaders of Iliyanbruen made peace with the human survivors of Illusk, setting a border between their kingdoms at the River Mirar.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 59
